record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Prove nontrivial results about the expected end-to-end distance of a self-avoiding walk in dimensions below 4, including whether it exceeds that of simple random walk, whether it has an exponent, and whether that exponent differs from 1/2.

evidence.quote: Prove anything at all about the expected end-to end distance of a self avoiding walk in d < 4. Is it greater than that of simple random walk? Does it have an exponent? If it does, is the exponent different from 1/2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 1$ be an integer and consider the hypercubic lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$. An $n$-step self-avoiding walk (SAW) starting at the origin is a sequence $\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \ldots, \omega_n)$ with $\omega_0 = 0$, $\omega_i \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, $|\omega_{i+1} - \omega_i| = 1$ for each $i$, and $\omega_i \neq \omega_j$ whenever $i \neq j$. Let $c_n$ denote the number of such $n$-step self-avoiding walks, and put the uniform probability measure on the set of $n$-step SAWs. Let
\[
\langle |\omega_n|^2 \rangle_{\text{SAW}} = \frac{1}{c_n} \sum_{\omega} |\omega_n|^2
\]
be the mean-square end-to-end distance of an $n$-step SAW. Let $\langle |S_n|^2 \rangle_{\text{SRW}} = n$ denote the same quantity for the simple symmetric random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$.

For dimensions $d < 4$, establish any of the following:

(a) Prove that $\langle |\omega_n|^2 \rangle_{\text{SAW}} \geq \langle |S_n|^2 \rangle_{\text{SRW}} = n$ for all sufficiently large $n$ (i.e., that the mean-square displacement of the SAW is at least that of the simple random walk).

(b) Prove that there exists a critical exponent $\nu = \nu(d) > 0$ such that
\[
\langle |\omega_n|^2 \rangle_{\text{SAW}} = n^{2\nu + o(1)} \qquad \text{as } n \to \infty.
\]

(c) Assuming such an exponent $\nu(d)$ exists, prove that $\nu(d) \neq 1/2$.
artifact.status_search_result:
For dimensions $d = 2, 3$ (below the upper critical dimension $4$), essentially nothing is rigorously known about the mean-square end-to-end distance of the self-avoiding walk. The existence of the critical exponent $
u(d)$ is not known, the conjectured values ($
u = 3/4$ in $d=2$, $
u \approx 0.5876$ in $d=3$) are unproven, and even the basic comparison that SAW spreads at least as fast as simple random walk is not established. Recent surveys (Bauerschmidt–Duminil-Copin–Goodman–Slade lectures; Duminil-Copin's lecture notes; arXiv:2207.08433) explicitly list these as open problems.

status_evidence.title: Lectures on Self-Avoiding Walks (Bauerschmidt-Duminil-Copin-Goodman-Slade)
status_evidence.snippet: For d = 2, 3, 4 almost nothing else has been proved. Notably, it is not even known that the mean-square displacement grows at least as rapidly as simple random walks and slower than ballistically.
status_evidence.claim: For d<4 the basic questions about SAW end-to-end distance remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of critical exponents for self-avoiding walks
status_evidence.snippet: It remains an open problem to prove the existence of the critical exponents for d = 2.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of the SAW critical exponent in low dimensions is open.

status_evidence.title: Self-avoiding walk - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: For d = 3 one only has a numerical estimate due to Clisby, ν = 0.587597 ± 0.000007.
status_evidence.claim: Only numerical estimates exist for the exponent in d=3.
